This is stated for both the orange and red lines. In both cases, the high plateau ends at layer 16, after which the values drop significantly. At layer 18, the values for the orange and red lines are already down to approximately 150 and 170, respectively, which is not 'high' compared to their peak near 500.

This description for the orange "atten_residual" line is an over-simplification. The line declines to ~150 at layer 18, but then continues to fall to a minimum of ~15 at layer 21 before rising again to a final value of ~200.

This description of the red "ffn_residual" line is highly inaccurate. While the line does have a local minimum around 120-130 at layer 21, it then rises sharply to a final value of approximately 310 at layer 24. The description completely misrepresents the final behavior and value of this line.

The initial rise starts after layer 17, it has a peak, then drops sharply back to near zero at layer 19, before rising again. The description misses this complex behavior, particularly the significant drop at layer 19.

The plot does not show four different gating configurations; it shows four different components (attn_output, attn_residual, ffn_output, ffn_residual) for a single configuration, as indicated by the title and legend. This information appears to be inferred from an external source (the paper's caption) and is not present in the figure itself.
The data on the x-axis extends beyond layer 22, with data points visible up to at least layer 23.
For the orange 'attn_residual' line, the value at layer 6 is approximately 410, not 450.
For the red 'ffn_residual' line, the value at layer 6 is approximately 410, not 480. This is a significant overestimation.
The description of the 'attn_residual' line omits its behavior after layer 20, where it rises again to a value of approximately 200 by layer 23.
The description of the 'ffn_residual' line omits its behavior after layer 20, where it rises sharply again to a value of approximately 310 by layer 23.

In the description of the 'ffn_output' line, it is stated that the line drops again after rising around layer 20. However, the plot shows the line is still rising at the end of the visible x-axis range and does not drop.

Describing the behavior of the 'attn_residual' and 'ffn_residual' lines after their initial sharp rise as 'fluctuates slightly' is inaccurate. The lines rise to a high peak and then form a plateau for about 10 layers. 'Plateaus' or 'remains high' would be a more accurate description.
